text:
maria: Quick heads-up: reproducible OkHttp call cancellations during exponential backoff in Kotlin sampleapp on Android 14. Setup: Retrofit + OkHttp, WorkManager background sync, auth refresh on 401. Happens when device locks and wifi flaps.

maria: Short logs:
I/OkHttp: --> POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/feature
W/OkHttp: callTimedOut: canceling
I/OkHttp: <-- HTTP FAILED: java.io.IOException: canceled
E/App: Token refresh started
I/OkHttp: --> POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/feature
I/OkHttp: <-- 401 Unauthorized
E/App: Token refresh done
I/OkHttp: <-- HTTP FAILED: java.io.IOException: canceled

maria: Our quick repro used an Interceptor with runBlocking delay for backoff. In prod we use a CallAdapter with suspend retries.

alex: runBlocking in interceptor will block OkHttp threads and interact badly with coroutine cancellation. Use suspendCancellableCoroutine around Call.enqueue and cont.invokeOnCancellation { cancel() } for explicit semantics.

ben: Also try disabling HTTP/2 (client.protocols = listOf(Protocol.HTTP_1_1)) — changing auth header mid-connection + multiplexing can cancel in-flight streams.

ciara: WorkManager may cancel worker scope when system stops background work. If backoff lives on that scope, cancellation will propagate to okhttp Call. Consider persisting retry state and rescheduling or using a supervisorScope that survives WorkManager cancellation.

nate: Quick repro tips: adb shell svc wifi disable while waiting, add EventListener to log callStart/callFailed ordering, try Dispatchers.IO vs Default for backoff.

maria: Plan: 1) switch repro to suspend wrapper for Calls, 2) toggle HTTP/2, 3) add EventListener traces, 4) test on Pixel/emu Android 13/14, 5) PR docs note if needed. Will post results.
